evidence.title: Moe Szyslak
evidence.text: Morris "Moe" Szyslak is a fictional character from the American animated television series "The Simpsons".

evidence.title: Moe Szyslak
evidence.text: He is voiced by Hank Azaria and first appeared in the series premiere episode "Simpsons Roasting on an Open Fire".

evidence.title: Moe Szyslak
evidence.text: Moe is the proprietor and bartender of Moe's Tavern, a Springfield bar frequented by Homer Simpson, Barney Gumble, Carl Carlson, Lenny Leonard, Sam, Larry, and others.

evidence.title: Homer Simpson
evidence.text: Homer Jay Simpson is a fictional character and the main protagonist of the American animated television series "The Simpsons" as the patriarch of the eponymous family.

evidence.title: Homer Simpson
evidence.text: He is voiced by Dan Castellaneta and first appeared on television, along with the rest of his family, in "The Tracey Ullman Show" short "Good Night" on April 19, 1987.

evidence.title: Homer Simpson
evidence.text: Homer was created and designed by cartoonist Matt Groening while he was waiting in the lobby of James L. Brooks' office.

evidence.title: Homer Simpson
evidence.text: Groening had been called to pitch a series of shorts based on his comic strip "Life in Hell" but instead decided to create a new set of characters.

evidence.title: Homer Simpson
evidence.text: He named the character after his father, Homer Groening.

evidence.title: Homer Simpson
evidence.text: After appearing for three seasons on "The Tracey Ullman Show", the Simpson family got their own series on Fox that debuted December 17, 1989.

evidence.title: Citizen Joe
evidence.text: "Citizen Joe" is the fifteenth episode for season eight of the Canadian-American military science fiction television series "Stargate SG-1".

evidence.title: Citizen Joe
evidence.text: The episode features known voice actor Dan Castellaneta, who voices Homer Simpson in "The Simpsons".

evidence.title: Citizen Joe
evidence.text: The episode was written by executive producer Robert C. Cooper, the episode was directed by Andy Mikita.

evidence.title: Citizen Joe
evidence.text: The episode received a below average Nielsen household rating and received no syndication rating to compare.

evidence.title: Citizen Joe
evidence.text: The episode got strong reviews from major media publishers worldwide.

evidence.title: Ned Flanders
evidence.text: Nedward "Ned" Flanders, Jr. is a recurring fictional character in the animated television series "The Simpsons".

evidence.title: Ned Flanders
evidence.text: He is voiced by Harry Shearer, and first appeared in the series premiere episode "Simpsons Roasting on an Open Fire".

evidence.title: Ned Flanders
evidence.text: He is the good-natured, cheery next-door neighbor to the Simpson family and is generally loathed by Homer Simpson.

evidence.title: Ned Flanders
evidence.text: A devout Evangelical Christian with an annoyingly perfect family, he is among the friendliest and most compassionate of Springfield's residents and is generally considered a pillar of the Springfield community.

evidence.title: Grampa Simpson
evidence.text: Abraham Jedediah Simpson II, often known as Grampa, is a fictional character in the animated television series "The Simpsons".

evidence.title: Grampa Simpson
evidence.text: He made his first appearance in the episode entitled "Grampa and the Kids", a Simpsons short on "The Tracey Ullman Show".

evidence.title: Grampa Simpson
evidence.text: Voiced by Dan Castellaneta, he is the father of Homer Simpson and the grandfather of Bart, Lisa and Maggie Simpson.

evidence.title: Grampa Simpson
evidence.text: In the 1000th issue of "Entertainment Weekly", Grampa was selected as the Grandpa for "The Perfect TV Family".

evidence.title: Girly Edition
evidence.text: "Girly Edition" is the twenty-first episode in the ninth season of the American animated television series "The Simpsons".

evidence.title: Girly Edition
evidence.text: It originally aired on the Fox network in the United States on April 19, 1998.

evidence.title: Girly Edition
evidence.text: In the episode, Lisa and Bart Simpson must co-anchor a new news program, though when Bart is seen as a more successful news anchor, Lisa becomes jealous and seeks revenge.

evidence.title: Girly Edition
evidence.text: Meanwhile, in the subplot, Homer Simpson gets a monkey helper because of his laziness.

evidence.title: Girly Edition
evidence.text: "Girly Edition" was the first episode written by Larry Doyle and was directed by Mark Kirkland.

evidence.title: Girly Edition
evidence.text: Much of the subplot was inspired by the film "Monkey Shines".

evidence.title: Girly Edition
evidence.text: Critics gave the episode positive reviews and it was well received by Lisa's voice actress Yeardley Smith.
